entity: U.S. Senate recorded (roll call) votes in calendar 2025: 659 total, second to 1976; 356 on nominations

sources.quote: Of the upper chamber's 659 roll call votes in 2025 — the second most in history, topped only by the Senate's 1976 tally — less than 20% were fully attended.
sources.searcher_note: Same number (659) and same ranking (second only to 1976); no nomination vote count

sources.quote: The Senate cast an abnormally high number of recorded votes overall, thanks not only to the record number of roll call votes on Trump's nominations
sources.searcher_note: Says record number of roll calls on nominations; also 338 of 577 GOP party-unity wins came on nominations; its 85.3% party-unity figure covers both chambers, not a crossover measure like ours

sources.quote: Roughly 54% of the Senate's votes through the third en bloc batch have been related to nominations
sources.searcher_note: Partisan office. Also says 655 votes through Dec 18, eclipsing every year but one since 1947; 54% of 655 is about 354, near our 356; describes the September en bloc rules change

sources.outlet: Office of Senate Majority Leader John Thune
sources.quote: 653 votes cast so far this year. Which dwarfs any year going back to 1989
sources.searcher_note: Floor remarks: 653 votes as of Dec 18; same page says only 1976 had more votes in eight decades checked

sources.quote: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), no nomination had been confirmed without a roll call vote through September of 2025.
sources.searcher_note: CRS on the September 2025 en bloc reinterpretation; predicts fewer nomination roll calls after it, gives no monthly counts (our 37.3 to 12.6 a month is not stated). congress.gov copy returned 403

sources.quote: Senate Democrats have forced more than 30% of the roll-call votes in 2026 – up from under 20% in 2025
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff. Senate votes more on nominations than legislation, largely party-line; nominations topped 60% of roll calls by end of 2024. notus.org URL redirects here

notes: Headline numbers (659 votes, second only to 1976) are reported by Bloomberg Government and echoed by Thune/GOP leader pages (653-655 as of Dec 18). Record nomination roll calls stated by Roll Call. Not found in any source: the 356 nomination-vote count, the 37.3 to 12.6 per month drop after the en bloc change, and the 41.5% vs 13.5% zero-crossover comparison. No source disagreeing with the 659 / 1976 ranking was found.
